How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as
noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record.
Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read. Your comments must be received by 5:00
P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
  Public Comment.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 4, 2024  1
   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, June 4, 2024

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Mayor Wu
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Wu, Vice Mayor Menchaca, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Harrington

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. LGBTQ+ PRIDE MONTH

  B. SAN GABRIEL VALLEY MOSQUITO & VECTOR CONTROL DISTRICT
  (SGVMVCD) PRESENTATION

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of May 21, 2024.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of May 21, 2024.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 4, 2024  2
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. STATEMENT OF INVESTMENT POLICY 2024-2025 [RESOLUTION NO. 24-
  35]

  California Government Code Section 53646 requires the annual review of the
  City’s Investment Policy at a regular meeting of the City Council. The
  requirement for an annual policy is also stated in the City’s Fiscal Sustainability
  Policy (adopted April 2019 in the interest of fiscal accountability).

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-35 adopting
  the 2024-2025 Statement of Investment Policy.

  D. REPLACEMENT OF THE COUNCIL CHAMBER MICROPHONES AND VOTING
  SYSTEM IN THE AMOUNT OF $28,925.39

  The City of San Gabriel started the Council Chamber upgrade project in 2020
  which included installation of new sound-processing equipment. The next
  phase of this project is the replacement of the current microphone and voting
  system with a modern and more efficient integrated digital audio and voting
  system. Funds are budgeted and available in the IT internal service special
  project account 124-707-30-99-099 (Council Chamber Upgrade). The total cost
  for the proposed agreement is $28,925.39.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize an award of this project to
  Sunset Audio/Video in the amount of $28,925.39 and authorize the City
  Manager to execute associated documents.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 4, 2024  3
   E. AWARD OF PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT FOR AN AMOUNT OF
  $91,531 WITH MGT CONSULTING FOR A COMPREHENSIVE
  CLASSIFICATION AND COMPENSATION STUDY

  At the request of each employee group during the last round of labor
  negotiations, the City agreed to conduct a citywide classification and
  compensation study. On December 19, 2024, staff released Request for
  Proposal (RFP) No. 23-20 for a comprehensive classification and compensation
  study of all 84 full-time positions listed on the City’s authorized position
  classification and salary schedule. The overall objective of the study is to update
  the City’s position classification and compensation system (i.e., policies,
  procedures, and schedules) to meet current regulatory requirements, best
  practices, organizational needs, and market conditions. The total cost of the
  project is expected to be no more than $91,531.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve a professional service
  agreement with MGT Consulting for a comprehensive classification and
  compensation study and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement.

  F. AGREEMENT WITH THE SAN GABRIEL VALLEY HUMANE SOCIETY FOR
  ANIMAL CARE AND CONTROL SERVICES FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025 IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $525,000

  The San Gabriel Valley Human Society (SGVHS) has provided animal care and
  control services to the community for many decades. The City’s most recent
  agreement with SGVHS, approved by the City Council on May 16, 2023, was an
  amendment to the agreement dated June 3, 2021, and has a term of one-year.
  With the existing amendment set to terminate on June 30, 2024, the SGVHS is
  requesting a new agreement to continue services for the City for Fiscal Year
  2024-2025, with a new compensation amount of $525,000, which has already
  been included in the proposed budget. Based on prior years, the license fee
  revenue for FY 2024-2025 is estimated at $39,000.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 4, 2024  4
   Staff recommends that the City Council approve the Agreement with the San
  Gabriel Valley Humane Society for Fiscal Year 2024-2025 in the amount of
  $525,000 and authorize the City Manager to execute said agreement.

  G. ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 24-27 APPROVING THE FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025
  SENATE BILL 1 ROAD REPAIR AND ACCOUNTABILITY ACT PROJECT LIST
  THAT WILL ALLOW THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL TO RECEIVE AN ESTIMATED
  $1,009,951

  Senate Bill 1 (SB1), also known as Road Repair and Accountability Act of 2017,
  provides the City of San Gabriel with access to funds for basic road
  maintenance, rehabilitation, and safety projects. Adoption of Resolution No.
  24-27 will allow the City to receive SB1 funding estimated by the State of
  California to be $1,009,951 for Fiscal Year 2024-2025. To qualify for funding
  under the Act, the City must adopt a list of eligible street improvement projects.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-27 and
  authorize the Public Works Director to file necessary documentation to satisfy
  Senate Bill 1 funding requirements and act as the authorized signatory for
  matters related to Fiscal Year 2024-2025 funding.

  H. COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT WITH LOS ANGELES COUNTY FOR A TRAFFIC
  SIGNAL SYNCHRONIZATION PROJECT ON MAIN STREET/LAS TUNAS
  DRIVE FROM HUNTINGTON DRIVE TO GOLDEN WEST AVENUE FOR AN
  ESTIMATED COST SHARE OF $361,500

  On behalf of the City of San Gabriel and with City Council’s approval, the Los
  Angeles County Department of Public Works (LACDPW) is set to perform a
  Traffic Signal Synchronization Project (TSSP) on Main Street/Las Tunas Drive
  arterial street route from Huntington Drive to Golden West Avenue, which is
  jurisdictionally shared among three cities – Alhambra, San Gabriel, and Temple
  City. Due to the scope and cost of the project, the County policy requires a
  Cooperative Agreement to be executed for the TSSP project. The estimated
  total cost of the project is $3,744,200 with San Gabriel’s estimated share cost
  to be $361,500. Out of this $361,500 cost to the City, $348,851.02 will be
  credited through the Federal Surface Transportation Program-Local (STP-L) to

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 4, 2024  5
   the County in lieu of a cash payment. The remaining balance of $12,648.98 will
  come from the City’s Traffic Impact Fees fund.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-36 to
  appropriate $12,648.98 from the Traffic Impact Fees Fund to account 122-800-
  40-97-736; authorize the City Manager to execute the Cooperative Agreement
  between the City and Los Angeles County and approve the assignment of
  $348,851.02 available Federal Surface Transportation Program-Local funds to
  the County in lieu of a cash payment and approve a purchase order with the
  County for $12,648.98 using Traffic Impact Fees funds from account 122-800-
  41-97-736.

  I. THEATRE FEE REDUCTION REQUEST BY SAN GABRIEL LION’S CLUB –
  THANKS USA CARE FAIR

  San Gabriel Lion’s Club has requested a waiver of rental fees for their upcoming
  community Thanks USA Care Fair event, scheduled to take place on June 22,
  2024, in the Mission Playhouse parking lot, Glass Room and lobby. The request
  is for a $2,900 reduction to reduce their rental cost to $2.50. The current rental
  subsidy account has sufficient funds to cover a recommended facility rental
  waiver of $1,615.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council grant a partial waiver of the San Gabriel
  Mission Playhouse rental fee in the amount of $1,615 for the June 22, 2024,
  Lion’s Club Thanks USA Care Fair event.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ADOPTION OF PROPOSED OPERATING BUDGET, CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT
  PROGRAM, POSITION CLASSIFICATION AND SALARY SCHEDULE, AND
  APPROPRIATIONS LIMIT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025 [RESOLUTION NOS.
  24-28, 24-29, 24-30, 24-31]

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 4, 2024  6
   The City Council will hold a public hearing to consider the adoption of the
  proposed operating budget, Capital Improvement Program (CIP), position
  classification and salary schedule, and appropriations limit for Fiscal Year 2024-
  2025. The general fund operating budget is balanced with a surplus of
  $575,000. Projected general fund revenue is $54,511,000 and proposed general
  fund expenditures are $53,937,000. The fiscal year 2024-2025 all funds
  proposed budget and Capital Improvement Program presents $85,484,000 in
  revenues and $82,446,000 in expenditures. The general fund has total revenues
  of $54,511,000 and total expenditures of $53,937,000, for a positive net change
  in fund balance of $575,000. New funding for Capital Improvement programs
  is proposed in the amount of $3,053,000.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council conduct a public hearing on the
  proposed 2024-2025 operating and capital improvement program budgets,
  position classification and salary schedule, and appropriation limit, and after
  receiving comments and testimony adopt the following resolutions:

  1. Resolution No. 24-28 adopting the 2024-2025 operating budget.
  2. Resolution No. 24-29 adopting the 2024-2025 Capital Improvement
  Program budget.
  3. Resolution No. 24-30 adopting the 2024-2025 authorized position
  classification and salary schedule.
  4. Resolution No. 24-31 establishing the 2024-2025 appropriations limit.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 708 ADDING SECTION 150.300 TO THE CITY OF
  SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE SETTING FORTH AN EXPEDITED,
  STREAMLINED PERMITTING PROCESS FOR ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING
  STATIONS AS REQUIRED BY GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 65850.7 –
  INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING

  In 2015, the State of California adopted Assembly Bill 1236 (2015, Chiu, codified
  as Government Code Section 65850.7), which requires local jurisdictions with a
  population less than 200,000 residents to adopt an ordinance to create an
  expedited, streamlined permitting process for electric vehicle charging stations.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 4, 2024  7
   An electric vehicle charging station is any level of electric vehicle supply
  equipment station that delivers electricity from a source outside an electric
  vehicle into a plug-in electric vehicle. The proposed ordinance is intended to
  bring the City of San Gabriel’s Municipal Code up to compliance with State
  legislation regarding the expediting and streamlining procedures for electric
  vehicle charging stations. There is no immediate financial impact or budget
  action necessary because of the recommended action.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council introduce Ordinance No. 708, adding
  Section 150.300 to the City of San Gabriel Municipal Code setting forth an
  expedited, streamlined permitting process for electric vehicle charging stations
  as required by Government Code Section 65850.7, by title only, waive future
  reading, and schedule the second reading and adoption for the next regularly-
  scheduled City Council meeting.

  B. APPROVAL OF AN AGREEMENT WITH ACE PARKING MANAGEMENT
  INCORPORATED FOR PARKING ENFORCEMENT SERVICES THROUGH JUNE
  2027 NOT TO EXCEED $1,249,668 FOR THE THREE-YEAR TERM

  The City has been in contract with Inter-Con Security Systems Inc. to provide
  parking-enforcement services since September 2018. The current contract
  expires on June 30, 2024. Parking-enforcement officers issue citations related
  to parking violations and complaints. Additionally, they respond to calls-for-
  service involving parking-related complaints during hours of service which
  alleviates the need for patrol officers to respond to these types of calls. Parking
  enforcement services are currently budgeted in the Police Department’s
  Contractual Services #121-751-00-22-000 in the amount of $350,000 for FY
  2024-2025 due to forecasted cost escalations.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter a
  three-year contract with Ace Parking, ending on June 30, 2027, with two
  additional one-year extensions that may be considered at the discretion of the
  City at the expiration of the three-year period.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 4, 2024  8
   C. FORMATION OF AN AD HOC SUBCOMMITTEE TO EXPLORE POLICIES AND
  PROGRAMS TO SUPPORT THE SAN GABRIEL LGBTQ+ COMMUNITY

  During the City Council meeting on April 16, 2024, the City Council directed
  staff to schedule an agenda item for the creation of an ad hoc subcommittee
  to discuss matters related to the San Gabriel LGBTQ+ community. The topics
  for discussion could include items such as how to recognize Pride Month in San
  Gabriel and to explore any programs or policies that the City could implement
  to support the San Gabriel LGBTQ+ community. This agenda item describes the
  parameters that guide an ad hoc subcommittee, considers the appointment of
  two City Councilmembers to a new ad hoc subcommittee, and proposes the
  focus of the new Ad Hoc Subcommittee. There is no fiscal impact associated
  with a discussion and creation of a City Council subcommittee, other than the
  staff time involved in supporting the subcommittee. Any future
  recommendations made to the City Council by the subcommittee will be
  analyzed for fiscal impact at the time they are considered by the City Council.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the Mayor appoint two Councilmembers to serve on a
  Council ad hoc subcommittee until recommendations are forwarded to the full
  Council or December 31, 2024, whichever comes first, to make
  recommendations to the full Council on potential programs and policies to
  support the City’s LGBTQ+ community.

  In addition to the recommended actions, the City Council has the following
  options:

  1. Decide to create a standing subcommittee instead of an ad hoc
  subcommittee and appoint two members to review all future items
  related to the City’s LGBTQ+ community.
  2. Decide not to create a subcommittee at this time.
  3. Some other action that the City Council decides based upon discussion
  at the meeting.

  D. CONSIDERATION OF RESOLUTIONS RELATING TO THE CALLING OF SAN
  GABRIEL’S GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION TO BE HELD ON NOVEMBER 5,
  2024 [RESOLUTIONS NOS. 24-32, 24-33, 24-34]

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 4, 2024  9
   This item calls the General Municipal Election for November 5, 2024, for the
  election of two members of the City Council; requests consolidation with the
  Statewide General Election and sets regulations for candidate statements.
  Funding for the November 2024 Consolidated Election is contained in the
  proposed General Fund Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Budget (Account Nos. 121-702-
  00-22-000 and 121-702-00-31-000). The cost of holding the election is
  estimated at $95,000.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the following resolutions:

  1. Resolution No. 24-32 calling for the holding of a General Municipal
  Election on Tuesday, November 5, 2024.
  2. Resolution No. 24-33 requesting the Board of Supervisors of the County
  of Los Angeles to consolidate, administer, manage, and oversee the
  Election.
  3. Resolution No. 24-34 establishing regulations for candidate statements;
  with or without the option for online candidate statements.

  E. CONSIDERATION OF FRIENDSHIP CITY PARTNERSHIP WITH BANQIAO
  DISTRICT IN NEW TAIPEI CITY, TAIWAN (REPUBLIC OF CHINA) AS WELL AS
  CONSIDERATION OF A CULTURAL EXCHANGE TRIP TO TAIWAN BY SAN
  GABRIEL REPRESENTATIVES

  The City has been approached by the Hakka Federation of USA with a request
  to establish a Friendship City Relationship between the City of San Gabriel and
  the Banqiao District of New Taipei City, Taiwan (Republic of China). Additionally,
  Mayor Wu has tentatively planned a trip to Taiwan for cultural exchange, disaster
  preparedness, tourism promotion, economic development, and smart city
  research with several cities and regions in Taiwan. There is no fiscal impact
  associated with entering into a Friendship City Agreement with the Banqiao
  District of New Taipei City. The fiscal impact of a cultural exchange trip to Taiwan
  is dependent on which option the City Council selects. The impact could range
  from $0 to $35,000 or more depending upon how many trips are paid for by the
  City.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 4, 2024  10
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve entering into a Friendship City partnership with the Banqiao
  District of New Taipei City, Taiwan (Republic of China).
  2. Authorize the Mayor to execute a Friendship City Agreement on behalf
  of San Gabriel.
  3. Provide direction on funding a trip to Taiwan.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, June 18, 2024 at
  6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be
  available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF JUNE 4, 2024
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Wu called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 6:30 P.M.
  on Tuesday, June 4, 2024, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive,
  San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Wu.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Vice Mayor
  Menchaca, and Mayor John Wu.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City Attorney
  Martin Koczanowicz, Community Services Director

I  Rebecca Perez, Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Finance Director William Kaholokula, Community
  Development Director Aldo Cervantes, Police Chief
  Edward Elizalde, Fire Division Chief Bradley Davis,
  Principal Civil Engineer Angela Cheng and Management
  Assistant Adam Yang.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  A. CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR (GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6)

  City Negotiators - City Manager Lazzaretto, City Attorney Lemieux, and Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Macias

  Regarding the following Employee Organizations - San Gabriel Police Officer's
  Association, San Gabriel Police Management Group, San Gabriel Firefighter's
  Association, San Gabriel Fire Management Group and all Unrepresented
  Employees.

I  Assistant City Attorney Koczanowicz announced that for the Special Meeting held
  on June 4, 2024, no reportable action was taken.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  request meeting agendas.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 8  June 4, 2024
   a

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Wu approved the agenda order.

  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. LGBTQ+ PRIDE MONTH

  Mayor Wu made the presentation and Douglas Chadwick, President/Executive
  Director Kiwanis Literacy Club Foundation and Kiwanis LGBTQ+ Charter Member,
  received the proclamation.

I  B. SAN GABRIEL VALLEY
  PRESENTATION
  MOSQUITO  &  VECTOR  CONTROL  DISTRICT

  District Director of Communications Anais Medina Diaz made the presentation.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Robert Powers provided comments in support of San Gabriel's Farmers Market.

  Florence Simpson, resident, expressed displeasure with the dissolution of the Human
  Equity, Access, and Relations Commission.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Regarding Item 4F, the following provided comments or spoke expressing concerns
  about management and current practices at the San Gabriel Valley Humane Society
  shelter: Cheryl Cabot, resident; Linda Perea; Mia Gutierrez; Robert Nichols; Cynthia

I  Talavera, resident; and Rachel Conger.

  City Manager Lazzaretto explained that the San Gabriel Valley Humane Society has a
  contractor relationship with the City, the City has no way to investigate them as a
  service provider, and the City purposely stays away from management of the shelter
  for liability purposes.

  Regarding Item 41, the following spoke in favor of the fee waiver: Charley Lu; and Mary
  He.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Harrington, to approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 41 as presented.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, HARRINGTON, MENCHACA, WU
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

I  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved:

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of May 21, 2024.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of May 21 , 2024.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 8  June 4, 2024
   The City Council approved May 10, 2024, and May 17, 2024, Registers of Demands
  and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  C. STATEMENT OF INVESTMENT POLICY 2024-2025 [RESOLUTION NO. 24-35]

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 24-35 adopting the 2024-2025
  Statement of Investment Policy.
